correctness.rationale: For quandle multiplication e_i e_j=e_(2j-i mod8), the reduction pi:R8→R4 is an algebra homomorphism. The characteristic-2 kernel is a right annihilator, so zero has only zero idempotent lift. Classifying R4 idempotents by even/odd coefficient sums yields the two disjoint affine two-planes downstairs. Direct expansion of any lift in the even family gives residual coefficients E0=h(t+1)+t²+t and E2=ht+t²+t, whose difference is h; hence h=0 and t in {0,1}, and the remaining odd equation imposes one free-variable equality. Translation by one yields two odd basis lifts, four affine three-spaces W0/W1 plus zero. This is an all-characteristic-two-fields symbolic proof, independently checked by enumerating every F2^8 and F4^8 coefficient tuple (33 and 257 actual idempotents) and predicted four affine fibers.
residual_risks: Finite q=2,4 counts are corroboration; proof for arbitrary infinite characteristic-two fields relies on polynomial equations.
General characteristic-two commutative coefficient rings and odd characteristic are not included.

originality.rationale: The exact R8 characteristic-two affine-fiber classification is not implied by the 2022 covering theorem: it assumes the quotient quandle ring has only trivial idempotents, while K[R4] has 1+2q². Its even-order corollary is for R_(2n) with odd n, not 8. Sangare–Ta characteristic-two claim assumes commutative quandles, and R8 is noncommutative. The 2026 Fourier study could still contain unadvertised characteristic-two implications; abstract-only access and Oxford VPN block remain a residual risk rather than an automatic originality failure.

value.rationale: This is the natural complete idempotent locus of the first nontrivial higher power-of-two dihedral quandle algebra in characteristic two. Four affine three-dimensional components and the exact failure of most R4 idempotents to lift give a meaningful covering/lifting obstruction, stronger than the finite-field number 1+4q³ alone.
residual_risks: No claim for arbitrary dihedral orders or general coefficient rings.
